children: Turkey's Financial Stability Committee on Thursday ruled out any structural risks to Turkish markets and said it would take measures to preserve financial stability, blaming recent volatility on credit and liquidity problems at funds managed by a limited number of portfolio management companies.
The committee's statement came after a sharp declines in Turkish stocks and steep falls in investment funds on Wednesday and early on Thursday prompted concern among regulators and investors.

Tera Portfoy, which manages about $13.7 billion in assets, said on Wednesday it had defaulted on redemption payments in its money market and equity fund, a day after Pusula Portfoy reported similar difficulties.
Tera Holding Chairman Emre Tezmen said the firm was facing a "planned, deliberate and organised speculative attack" and described the liquidity problems as temporary.

The Financial Stability Committee said, "the problem is concentrated in a specific segment of the fund market and is temporary and manageable in nature...measures will primarily focus on easing liquidity constraints and preventing contagion risk," the committee said.
Regulatory and supervisory authorities will continue to exercise their powers decisively against those found to have engaged in market-disruptive actions, the committee said.

Separately, Turkey's central bank said it would increase funding provided through one-week repo auctions, revise banks' borrowing limits and reduce collateral haircuts in the light of recent volatility.

Turkey's benchmark BIST-100 index reversed early losses to rise 2% at 0815 GMT, led by a 6% jump in banking shares, while Tera Yatirim Menkul Degerler and Tera Yatirim Teknoloji Holding fell 10% after sharp declines in the previous session.
index fell over 5.5% on Wednesday's close, recording its biggest daily loss since May.

Separately, Turkey's Capital Markets Board on Wednesday filed criminal complaints against 38 people and imposed two-year trading bans to people including fund manager Pusula Portfoy and its executives over alleged manipulation of shares in three listed companies.
